text:
ryan_ae: Heads-up  New Acme Health POC: procurement says they can wire today to speed close. Legal flagged wire-before-countersign as high risk. Can we offer a pragmatic compromise?

maria_legal: Short answer: we prefer DocuSign. Compromise options: (A) wire to Redwood with a 10% holdback and exec email authorization + PO with tax ID; (B) wire to escrow (slower; bank setup). If they insist on wire-first we need explicit wiring_authorization language on the PO and buyer exec approval.

frank_fin: Finance can do the 10% holdback. Requirements: PO must include po_number, bill_to entity, tax_id, amount, currency, wiring_authorization text and remittance instructions. Example remittance note: "Wire conditioned on countersigned MSA/DPA or buyer exec email confirming authorization."

anya_se: For the POC we'll need Dedicated pool + KMS attestation. We can deliver a signed attestation PDF and the SecQ answers by EOD. Note: customer-managed HSM is supported but onboarding is 2-3 weeks and will only start after contract flow confirmation. If they wire before countersign, HSM provisioning may be delayed.

ryan_ae: They also pushed on the SLA: asking for 30% credit if outage >1h. Our standard is monthly cap 25% and single-incident cap 10%. Can legal keep that?

maria_legal: Recommend standard SLA language. Draft clause: "Service credits up to 25% of monthly charges; per-incident credits capped at 10% of monthly charges. Uptime measured by Redwood telemetry per SLA appendix." Add exclusions: customer misconfiguration and force majeure.

frank_fin: Also call out billing trigger for reserved capacity. Sales suggested "1-month reserved pool starts on first production token". Finance prefers a clear invoiceable trigger (countersign date or provisioning complete). We should pick one to avoid disputes.

anya_se: Technical view: we provision infra when orderform countersign is complete and infra config is approved. Billing on first production token aligns with usage, but provisioning might occur earlier. Suggest: "billing starts on first production token or 14 days after countersign, whichever comes first." Open to legal input.

maria_legal: That hybrid trigger seems fine, but tighten wording: define "production token" and include a maximum free provisioning window (e.g., 14 days) to prevent ambiguous charges. I'll add the clause to the order form redline.

ryan_ae: Procurement asked for a PO template to feed into their ERP. Frank, can you paste a minimal PO payload we can share?

frank_fin: Minimal PO payload (share to procurement):
```
po_number: PO-ACME-2024-1201
amount: 95000.00
currency: USD
tax_id: 12-3456789
bill_to: Redwood Inference LLC
wiring_authorization: "Buyer authorizes wire to Redwood account; funds conditioned on countersigned MSA/DPA or buyer exec email confirming authorization."
notes: "Attach countersigned MSA or reference countersign workflow"
```

drive-bot: Uploaded orderform_holdback_v1.pdf and msa_dpa_redline_holdback.docx to drive: https://redwood.co/drive/acme-poc (perms: sales,legal,finance).

maria_legal: I'll add a short FAQ for procurement outlining acceptable wire flows, PO fields, and the wet-ink fallback (mailing address, signatory name/title, retention of originals). Recommend we push DocuSign for speed; accept wet-ink only if customer legal requires it.

anya_se: I'll finish the KMS attestation and SecQ answers tonight and ping legal to attach to the redline.

ryan_ae: Thanks team  I'll propose the 10% holdback + exec email + PO today and offer DocuSign as the preferred fast path. Tagging @maria_legal @frank_fin @anya_se. :thumbsup:
